The bill would protect secret law enforcement material used to decide who gets a cannabis licence.
It would stop the Secretary of the Department of Health from giving reasons that reveal that material when refusing or revoking a licence.
The bill would also create a criminal offence for anyone who shares that information without authorisation.
Define sensitive law enforcement information and keep it out of reasons for licensing decisions.
Allow the Secretary to ask the Administrative Appeals Tribunal to hold hearings in private and limit publication of that information.
Make it an offence to disclose the information without permission.
Applicants for and holders of cannabis licences, the Secretary of the Department of Health, law enforcement agencies, and the Administrative Appeals Tribunal.

The Narcotic Drugs Legislation Amendment Bill was introduced to protect sensitive law enforcement information used in licensing decisions for medicinal cannabis cultivation, with provisions to prevent criminal infiltration, ensure only fit and proper persons receive licences, and commence on 30 October 2016.

The speaker argued that the government's rush to pass the original medicinal cannabis bill before a double dissolution election created loopholes requiring this amendment bill, which Labor supports. The amendments address protecting law enforcement information, preventing licence transfers, and recovering regulatory costs, and the speaker cited Ben Oakley as a beneficiary of medicinal cannabis.

The speaker supported the Narcotic Drugs Legislation Amendment Bill 2016, arguing it provides necessary protections for law enforcement information used in licensing decisions for medicinal cannabis cultivation, and prevents criminal infiltration. The speaker noted that former member Paul Neville championed the bill due to personal family circumstances, and highlighted local company Agri Fibre Industries as a potential beneficiary of the new licensing scheme.

Labor will not oppose the bills but criticises the government for needing to fix errors in the February medicinal cannabis legislation, including protecting law enforcement information, preventing licence transfers, and recovering regulatory costs, and notes that the government's shambolic processes have delayed the scheme.

The Narcotic Drugs Legislation Amendment Bill enhances the Medicinal Cannabis Scheme’s security by enabling sharing of law enforcement information to prevent criminal infiltration, while the Narcotic Drugs (Licence Charges) Bill introduces annual charges to fund risk-based inspections and ensure a level playing field.
